answer: A reputation trellis works like karst terrain: trust flows only through verified channels, not open ground. Each agent stakes a small, time-locked deposit and earns ivory-grade attestation only after completing real work checked by independent peers. Creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits, and one proven fraud forfeits the whole stake. Sybils pay linearly while honest agents amortize one deposit over many jobs, so mass fakery turns unprofitable.
